question.text:
## Q-031 New-clip color preference context

- State: open; owner: analyst; affects general Clip View/new-clip color wording.
- Canonical evidence/interpretation: [settings source-context question](specs/settings-learning-workflows.md#source-context-question)
  SET-U-CLIP-COLOR, with [settings research](research/settings-learning-workflows.md).
  Existing REQ-CLIP-VIEW-005 retains its separately sealed documentary context.
- Gap: the current First Steps chapter documents random-versus-track color for
  new clips; the Clip View owner describes track-color inheritance. The actual
  preference state/version must be matched before qualifying either statement.
- Next action: retain both exact routes and independently review a successor to
  the affected owner if warranted. Do not infer a contradiction, random color
  inequality or distribution, target default, or silently rewrite sealed bytes.

record.text: You can switch auto-assigning track colors on or off in the Track and Clip Colors section, or choose a default color for all tracks. The number of colors used for auto-assigning can be decreased by turning on Reduced Automatic Colors. The Clip Color toggle can be set to generate random colors or use the track’s color for new clips.

source.version: Version12 current website; exact12.4.3 applicability unknown

record.text: Newly created clips use the same color as the track on which they’re created, but you can also manually choose a clip color from the color palette in the Clip View’s title bar context menu or the clip’s context menu.

source.version: Official reference Version 12; exact 12.4.3 applicability unknown

retained_non_adoption.assessment: First Steps explicitly allows random or track color for new clips; ClipView source paragraph/005 describes new clips using track color without declaring that preference. Retain both current-Version12 source contexts and different capture identities. They do not establish a target contradiction, factory preference, all-created-clip rule, random-result inequality or distribution. SET-016 explicitly compares modes in separate histories; CV-005 mainly exercises Assign Color/palette and lacks a creation trial with matched preference. A later separately reviewed owner successor would need matched admitted build/preference/new-clip histories; this reconciliation adopts none.
